system.io.util.ref: vendor: fixtures/datadog/otel-mapping.yaml has no row for system.io.util. DERIVED: rebuilt as 100 x rate(system.disk.io_time); both read the same kernel busy-time counter. datadog: Agent core check io, https://github.com/DataDog/datadog-agent/blob/6c2b9607c8acba411a489492edeaa14bd5e98106/pkg/collector/corechecks/system/disk/io/iostats_nix.go: gopsutil disk.IOCounters per device (tags device, device_name), util = delta(IoTime ms) / (delta ms / 10) * 100, submitted as Gauge system.io.util = util/10.0, i.e. percent of wall time the device was busy (sysstat %util); https://docs.datadoghq.com/integrations/system/#metrics: gauge, unit percent. otel: fixtures/otel/collector-contrib/receiver/hostmetricsreceiver/internal/scraper/diskscraper/metadata.yaml system.disk.io_time 'Time disk spent activated', sum monotonic cumulative, unit s, attribute device; https://github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-collector-contrib/blob/f56f9a38c9864e892af542f1dbd28f475d6779dc/receiver/hostmetricsreceiver/internal/scraper/diskscraper/disk_scraper_others.go records precision.Scale(ioCounter.IoTime, time.Millisecond), the same gopsutil field in seconds. rate() gives busy seconds per second (0-1); scale 100 gives percent. type deviation: Datadog stores a percent gauge without a per-second unit, but it is computed from the IoTime counter delta, so kind rate. Device set: Datadog excludes devices only via device_exclude_re (iostats.go, no default); the disk scraper includes every device unless configured; the fixture averages over all devices. Differences: Datadog rounds and uses its check interval, rate() uses the window. rateWindow 5m: hostmetrics series arrive every 60 s, as measured for system.net.bytes_rcvd in this file (not re-measured for system.disk.io_time). otel_scope_name matcher as in the other host entries. No device label mapping: the fixtures only filter by $scope. dash0: not checked (no access in this run).

Why not the vendor row (sum of system.memory.usage over state): on Linux the scraper records used, free, buffered, cached, slab_reclaimable, slab_unreclaimable (memory_scraper_linux.go); gopsutil adds SReclaimable into Cached (https://github.com/shirou/gopsutil/blob/v4.26.10/mem/mem_linux.go 'ret.Cached += ret.Sreclaimable'), so slab_reclaimable is counted twice and slab_unreclaimable is already inside used; and the feature gate receiver.hostmetricsreceiver.UseLinuxMemAvailable (fixtures/otel/collector-contrib/receiver/hostmetricsreceiver/metadata.yaml, stage beta = on by default since v0.137.0) sets used = Total - MemAvailable, so even used+free+buffered+cached != Total. inactive is only emitted on non-Linux (memory_scraper_others.go: used, free, inactive). scale 9.5367431640625e-07 = 1/1048576: Datadog MiB vs OTel bytes.
